at: She doesn’t laugh. Then she very nearly does
alt: In the palace garden the princess very nearly laughs at the madman, and is furious about it.
scene: Close-up over Bihyung's shoulder: his blurred dark shoulder and the one stray strand of his hair fill the left foreground, out of focus. Razor-sharp in the midground, Princess Chunmyung at seventeen, in Sacred Bone silk and her binyeo, biting the inside of her cheek, eyes bright, the corner of her mouth losing the fight against a laugh. Behind her the palace garden melts into creamy bokeh: plum blossom, a stone lantern, sun through leaves. Late golden light rakes her face from the side.

at: Once she makes him laugh on the beat instead of after it.
alt: On the Ghost Bridge she makes him laugh on the beat for the first time, and neither of them says anything for the rest of the night.
scene: Intimate two-shot, very close, on the Ghost Bridge at night. Foreground: the small clay oil lamp she brought, sharp flame, its glow the only key. Midground, sharp: Chunmyung and Bihyung sitting shoulder to shoulder on the stones, both caught mid-laugh and suddenly staring at each other in surprise, faces inches apart, her hand frozen on his wax tablet. Background: black water with drifting lamp reflections and fireflies dissolving into bokeh discs. Warm lamplight from below on both faces.

at: Then it’s unanimous. Say yes.
alt: Then it's unanimous. Say yes. My feet are cold.
scene: Extreme close two-shot on the bridge at night, low angle. Chunmyung has a fist in Bihyung's collar, pulling him down to her height, chin up, blushing furiously, eyes fierce and wet. Bihyung looks down at her, the madness gone from his face, utterly undone, normal dark eyes. Foreground: the blurred edge of her silk sleeve and the lamp flame. Background: the crooked bridge parapet and the temple roof melting into moon-blue bokeh. Breath visible in the cold.

at: He comes back the next night. So does she.
alt: Legend: the goblins of Surabol hold lanterns along the Ghost Bridge for the madman and his princess.
scene: LEGEND VARIANT of the intro-card look (the story as the city believes it, told as real): cooler moon-blue palette, drifting silver mist, floating lantern motes, slightly heightened folk-tale staging; the dokkaebi are truly supernatural. Wide low shot along the Ghost Bridge: Chunmyung and Bihyung walk toward each other in the middle, small and sharp, about to meet. Lining both parapets, the dokkaebi of the attached spirit boards hold up paper lanterns for them: the three masked rascal goblins with smoke hair, the Old Man Tree with hollow wooden face, the Rock Lady with her stone crown. Foreground: a giant out-of-focus lantern and reeds at the lens. Background: mist and floating lantern bokeh over black water.
refsNote: dokkaebi spirit designs: copy each spirit's exact look

at: She puts her hand over his mouth.
alt: The first night in the house by the stream, she puts her hand over his mouth before he can tell the rafters about his day.
scene: Intimate close-up in a small dark room, lying down, camera at pillow height. Chunmyung, hair loose from her binyeo, propped on one elbow, lays her palm over Bihyung's mouth, smiling, eyes soft. Above her hand his eyes, normal and dark, crinkling, quieted. Foreground: the blurred curve of a quilt and a single candle flame at the lens edge. Background: rafters and paper door dissolving into warm umber bokeh. One candle key from the side. Tender, chaste, close.

at: It is the only room in Surabol where he never once performs.
alt: Legend: neighbours press their ears to the wall for goblins; on the roof, the goblins themselves keep watch over the couple.
scene: LEGEND VARIANT of the intro-card look (the story as the city believes it, told as real): cooler moon-blue palette, drifting silver mist, floating motes; the dokkaebi are truly supernatural. Night outside a small house by a stream. Foreground, out of focus: two neighbours in plain white with topknots pressing their ears to the mud wall. Midground, sharp: on the thatched roof ridge the three masked rascal goblins of the attached spirit board sit in a row with their smoke hair drifting, fingers to their lips, shushing. Warm light glows through the paper window below them. Background: stream and mist melting into moonlit bokeh.
refsNote: dokkaebi spirit designs: copy their exact look

at: They are buried on the same day, on the hill west of the stream
alt: Old Yongsu and Chunmyung die side by side in the same bed, holding hands, looking into each other's eyes.
scene: Very romantic, very close. Camera at pillow height across one bed. An old couple lie on their sides facing each other under one quilt in the small room by the stream: Kim Yongsu, white-haired, deeply lined, the one stray strand of hair still poking up; Chunmyung, grey-haired and beautiful in old age, her binyeo on the pillow beside her. Their hands are clasped between them on the quilt, fingers laced. They look into each other's eyes, tearful and smiling, at peace. Foreground: a blurred guttering candle and a sprig of plum blossom at the lens. Background: the paper door glowing with dawn, dissolving into soft gold bokeh. Warm candle key raking their faces and the laced hands.

at: Afterwards he walks down to the stream alone.
alt: Legend: on their last night the goblins come in from the reeds and kneel at the foot of the bed with lanterns.
scene: LEGEND VARIANT of the intro-card look (the story as the city believes it, told as real): cooler moon-blue palette, drifting silver mist, floating lantern motes, slightly heightened folk-tale staging; the dokkaebi are truly supernatural. Wide low shot inside the small room by the stream at night: the old couple lie in one bed holding hands, faces turned to each other, his eyes gone solid white, hers closed and smiling. At the foot of the bed, kneeling in silence with lowered paper lanterns, the dokkaebi of the attached spirit boards: three masked rascal goblins, the Old Man Tree, the Rock Lady. Plum petals drift through the open paper door. Foreground: a blurred lantern at the lens. Background: the open door to the moonlit stream and the Ghost Bridge, in mist bokeh.
refsNote: dokkaebi spirit designs: copy each spirit's exact look

at: Some nights the madman climbs the gate tower
alt: The madman and the goblin clerk sit on the gate-tower roof with their legs over the edge.
scene: Low angle from the street up at a tall timber gate tower at night. On the curved giwa roof, legs dangling over the edge, sit Bihyung and Gildal (fox mask pushed up on his head, orange robe), sharing a jar of wine, laughing. Foreground: blurred eave tiles and a hanging lantern right at the lens. Background: the moon and the roofs of Surabol dissolving into lantern bokeh and haze. Moonlight key with a warm lantern bounce on their faces.

at: I have never once been late.
alt: Gildal: I'll wait as long as you like. I have never once been late.
scene: Tight close-up of Gildal at night on the gate tower: fox mask pushed up on his head, orange robe, a faint smile and tired, loyal, waiting eyes looking off-frame at Bihyung. Foreground: the blurred shoulder and stray hair strand of Bihyung at the lens. Background: city roofs and lanterns melting into round bokeh. One lantern key on his face, deep shadows.

at: One morning the gate is empty, and a fox is running down the road
alt: Legend: the goblins drag the fox back through the reeds to the madman.
scene: LEGEND VARIANT of the intro-card look (the story as the city believes it, told as real): cooler moon-blue palette, drifting mist, heightened folk-tale staging; the dokkaebi are truly supernatural. Night in the reeds by the river. The dokkaebi of the attached spirit boards drag Gildal in his fox-dokkaebi form (copied exactly from his fox board) through the reeds by his orange robe; his log club trails in the mud. Waiting, sharp in the midground, Bihyung stands with his EYES SOLID WHITE, face unreadable. Foreground: blurred reed heads at the lens. Background: the palace wall and moon in mist bokeh.

at: He was late.
alt: The reality: Gildal dies in the reeds, his fox mask in the mud, the madman kneeling beside him.
scene: Emotional close shot, low in the mud of the reeds at grey dawn. Gildal (copied from his portrait: orange robe, red hood) lies dying on his back, bloody-faced, his fox mask fallen beside his head in the mud, looking up with something like apology. Bihyung kneels over him, holding his hand, face wrecked, normal dark eyes full of tears. Standing behind them, out of focus and silent, the real people of the attached human boards: three orphan boys with goblin masks round their necks, the one-eyed old stonecutter with his staff. Foreground: the blurred fox mask and reed stems at the lens. Background: river mist dissolving into pale grey bokeh. One cold dawn key.
refsNote: the real people behind the goblin legend: copy each exactly

at: three people eat supper at a table built for twelve
alt: Prince Suulbu eats supper with his wife and daughter at a table built for twelve.
scene: Low dramatic shot down the length of a long lacquered table built for twelve, in a rich dark hall. At the far head, sharp, Prince Suulbu in fine court silk, chewing, cold and calculating, eyes narrowed. Partway down one side, small, his daughter Manmyung and his wife, eating in silence. Nine empty places between them. Foreground: a blurred silver wine ewer and lamp flame at the lens. Background: a painted screen and lattice dissolving into umber bokeh. One lamp key, deep tenebrist shadows.

at: Suulbu opens his mouth. Nothing comes out.
alt: King Jinpyung turns Suulbu's own secret on him, and the High Councillor loses a sentence for the only time in his life.
scene: Tense close two-shot in the palace garden. Foreground left, out of focus: King Jinpyung's shoulder and crown. Razor-sharp in the midground: Prince Suulbu, the High Councillor, in fine silk and black feather cap, mouth open, nothing coming out, a vein at his temple, eyes flicking. Behind him, the garden in bokeh. A hard side key of afternoon sun splits his face into light and shadow.

at: …You were never mad. Were you.
alt: Ninety years old in his carried chair, Suulbu finally sees it: you were never mad, were you.
scene: Close two-shot at a feast doorway at night. Prince Suulbu, very old and shrunken in a carried chair, leans forward with a hard, frightened, admiring stare. Kim Yongsu, middle-aged, stray strand of hair, stands at the door looking back at him with perfectly sane, calm eyes and the faintest smile. Foreground: the blurred carrying pole and a bearer's hand. Background: the wedding hall, musicians and lanterns dissolving into warm bokeh. Lantern key from the side.

at: His father is not in chains. His father is on his knees, and talking.
alt: Under the canopy in the pines, the king of Golden Gaya kneels before the king of Silla; his son listens behind a pine.
scene: Over-the-shoulder from behind a pine trunk, the bark huge, dark and out of focus in the foreground. Midground through the trunks: in a clearing under a white canopy, King Beopheung of Silla sits on a camp chair, crowned, calm, a buyer; King Guhae of Golden Gaya kneels on the needles before him in his crown, hands open, pleading. Silla guards in steel lamellar at the edge. At the left edge, half hidden behind the pine and razor sharp, the adult Muryuk, a grown warrior in his prime, in steel lamellar and a tall conical Gaya helm, blood to the elbow, ring-pommel sword hanging from his fist, his face crumpling. Smoke from the burning harbour drifts through the trunks behind; one gold shaft on the two kings, bokeh of embers in the haze.

at: Men forget what a king says at the end of a war.
alt: Guhae on his knees: write it down, Majesty.
scene: Tight emotional close-up of King Guhae of Golden Gaya kneeling, crown slightly askew, tears in his eyes but his jaw set, looking up past the lens. Foreground: the blurred brush and paper on a camp table in Beopheung's hand. Background: pines, the white canopy and harbour smoke dissolving into bokeh. Gold shaft of light across his face.

at: By noon the Gaya line has broken on the riverbank.
alt: Muryuk holds the ford with his father's guard at his back while the Gaya line breaks.
scene: Battle mid-moment, worm's-eye from the churning water of a river ford. Muryuk, adult, in steel lamellar and tall conical Gaya helm, purple cloth at the collar, shouting, ring-pommel sword raised, stands in thigh-deep water with a handful of Gaya guards behind him. Silla spearmen in blue cloth surge at them through spray. Foreground: a blurred spear point and splashing water at the lens. Background: the harbour iron sheds burning, black smoke columns, embers drifting into bokeh.

at: He walks up the gate road bareheaded, the helm in his hand.
alt: At Great Gaya, Muryuk walks up the gate road bareheaded, his helm in his hand, and every bow on the wall finds him.
scene: Over-the-shoulder from the Great Gaya wall: foreground, a blurred Gaya archer's drawn bow and arrow tip at the lens. Midground, sharp, down the gate road: Muryuk, grey at the temples, in steel lamellar on the Silla side, bareheaded, walking slowly up toward the gate with his tall conical Gaya helm in his hand, face calm and grieving. Background: the Silla army behind him as massed painted shapes in dust haze, blue banners dissolving into bokeh.

at: five thousand horse go through the
alt: While every bow is on Muryuk, fifteen-year-old Sadaham takes five thousand horse through the gate.
scene: Battle mid-moment, low dutch angle inside the gate passage of Great Gaya. Fifteen-year-old Sadaham on a charging horse bursts through the open gate leaves toward the lens, sword forward, ice-blue cloth streaming, cavalry pouring behind him. Foreground: a blurred falling gate bar and flying splinters at the lens. Background: dust, fire and sparks in bokeh. Horse with full readable body, modelled muscle, edge light along the topline.

at: He finds the old lords of Great Gaya in the hall
alt: Muryuk finds the old lords of Great Gaya sitting very straight in their hall, ready to die well.
scene: Inside a dim Gaya hall, smoke drifting in. Foreground: Muryuk's blurred armoured shoulder and helm at the lens. Midground, sharp: a row of old Gaya lords in fine purple and white robes sitting very straight on their mats, faces composed, one old man looking straight at Muryuk. Background: the open doors full of fire and smoke, ember bokeh. One hard fire key from the doorway.

at: Get up, all of you. The lane’s wet.
alt: Gaya smiths kneel to their old king in a wet Surabol lane; he tells them to bow to the king up the hill.
scene: Rainy morning in a narrow Surabol lane. Foreground: a blurred kneeling smith's soot-black back and wet shoulder at the lens. Midground, sharp: Kim Guhae, now in plain Silla dress and black feather cap, bending to lift another kneeling smith by the elbow, kind and stern. Behind him a few more Gaya smiths in leather aprons kneel in the puddles. Background: the Moon Palace roofs up the hill in rain haze and bokeh. Cool rain light with a warm forge glow from a doorway.

at: never turns his head. Muryuk turns his every time.
alt: Iron-seller! Guhae walks past the hecklers without turning his head; Muryuk turns his every time.
scene: Street, morning, telephoto compression. Foreground: blurred jeering Silla youths' arms and mouths at the lens edge. Midground, sharp: Kim Guhae walking uphill, eyes front, serene, in councillor dress; one step behind him the adult Muryuk, jaw clenched, head turned toward the hecklers with a killing look. Background: the lane and palace roofs dissolving into hazy bokeh. Low side sun.
